### Added
- **`core_auth_status` reads every server's sign-in state, and issues the links that start the missing grants.** A client that gets a person ready before the agent needs them (a chat front-end after its sign-in) needed one `core_auth_login` per server to learn a link, and `auth://status` named no link. The new read-only core tool answers the `auth://status` document for the caller; with `auth_urls: true` every server waiting for the person's grant carries its sign-in link (`auth_url`), and a server whose grant the person already holds is connected and reported `connected`. Each entry of both now says how the person reaches the server (`kind`: `grant`, `sso` or `none`) and, for a grant, whom it belongs to (`grant_scope`: `subject` or `session`). ([#1507](https://github.com/giantswarm/muster/issues/1507))
### Fixed
- **A server that needs the person's grant reports `auth_required` before its issuer is known.** A pending-auth server rebuilt from its service's own data carries no 401-time auth info until a login discovers it, and `auth://status` reported it `disconnected` with no `auth_tool`: a client listing what the person must connect left it out. An OAuth server that neither forwards nor exchanges the person's token now reports `auth_required` with `core_auth_login` and, where the MCPServer pins one, its issuer. ([#1507](https://github.com/giantswarm/muster/issues/1507))
